active_stories.headline: Frontier unit economics collide: Fable 5.1 cache cut vs Astra Fast surcharge vs Gemini 3.8 Flash intro cliff
active_stories.claim: September 2026 frontier releases are rewriting agentic unit economics more than headline benchmarks: Fable 5.1 keeps $10/$50 list but cuts cache reads to $0.25/M; GPT-6 Astra lists at $10/$50 (Fast mode 2× on short-context tokens); Gemini 3.8 Flash holds $0.75/$3.75 intro through 2026-12-31 then doubles to $1.50/$7.50.
active_stories.one_sentence_take: Three verified pricing regimes landed in days — which becomes the default agentic spend lane this quarter is Contested between economics and capability/harness claims.
bullets: Primary: Anthropic — Fable 5.1 $10/$50; cache reads $0.25/M (75% cut); vendor estimates ~25% typical / ~45% highly agentic savings vs Fable 5.
Primary: OpenAI pricing — gpt-6-astra short-context $10/$50; Fast mode priced at 2× ($20/$100); cached input $1.00/M (4× Fable cache reads).
Primary: Google — Gemini 3.8 Flash intro $0.75/$3.75 through 2026-12-31; standard $1.50/$7.50 from 2027-01-01 (blog + API pricing page).
Specialist tension: list-price winner (Flash) can lose on cost-per-task if token intensity rises; Fable cache economics win only with high hit rates / stable prefixes.
Decision surface stays open: build/buy/ship default for agentic production spend — not settled by benches alone.
active_stories.explainer: CIO pressure-test (2026-09-16): three-lane price facts corroborate across independent Primary pages. Contested is the decision frame — whether cache/intro/Fast economics dominate lane choice (Leg A) or capability/harness/distribution claims dominate and pricing is noise (Leg B). No averaged 'winner.' High is withheld on the decision; price facts alone would clear High.
active_stories.point: Unit economics moved in footnotes (cache, Fast, intro cliffs) as much as in model cards.
active_stories.motive: Labs want share of agentic spend; buyers want cost-per-task certainty before locking a default stack.
active_stories.bottom_line: Recalculate cost-per-task with your cache-hit and token-intensity profile before naming a default — list price alone misleads.

self_kill_attempt.claim_we_might_be_wrong: The 'unit economics rewrite defaults' frame overstates decision impact: Flash already wins list price by ~10× so the Sep moves are incremental not regime-changing for cost buyers; Fable's 25–45% savings are vendor-estimated on one usage mix; Astra Fast 2× is optional; and much agentic spend may ride seat licenses / cloud credits / distribution, not raw API list — so pricing footnotes may be noise vs capability/harness/distribution (Leg B wins by default without Contested theater).
evidence_that_would_retire_it: Primary share or procurement data showing default agentic production lanes chosen by non-API instruments (seats, credits, exclusive distribution) with list price inert
Primary pricing pages retract or contradict the three-lane numbers
Independent same-harness cost-per-task across Fable/Astra/Flash showing lanes converge within noise so economics cannot displace capability
self_kill_attempt.outcome_note: Job B falsify upgrade (TBL). Pricing Primaries still corroborate three-lane numbers — pricing_contradiction kill fails. kill_LegA fails — no Primary procurement share proving list price inert; OpenAI Enterprise token-based rate card cuts the other way. Hold Contested: Legs A/B both live; confidence null; never averaged. Gap remains: no independent same-harness cost-per-task jointly including Fable 5.1 + Astra + Flash. EXAMPLE stays retired (example:false). Hunt: data/tbl_job_b_falsify_hunt.json.
